title: lazy allgather splitter + priority NCCL streams to improve TP overlap and KV-cache throughput
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Introduce lazy allgather splitter and NCCL priority stream assignment to improve multi-GPU tensor-parallel throughput and reduce tail latency; default scheduler heuristic updated; opt-in via runtime flag rtp.lazy_allgather=true.
description: Context: tensor-parallel workloads at longer sequence lengths saw pronounced tail latency and KV-cache stalls when single large allgather operations saturated NCCL and serialized with compute. This PR introduces two coordinated changes: 1) a lazy allgather splitter that slices large allgathers into subwindows sized by runtime sequence-length histograms and active KV entries, enabling earlier progressive availability of KV shards to compute lanes; 2) a priority NCCL stream allocator and scheduler that pins small/latency-sensitive chunks to high-priority comm streams while routing bulk aggregation to background streams. Motivation: reduce head-of-line blocking, increase overlap between comm and compute, and reduce NCCL stream stalls on multi-node, multi-GPU clusters. Design summary: lazy splitter observes per-request prefix lengths and dynamic KV usage; it produces ordered chunk descriptors dispatched as separate NCCL allgather ops. A lightweight combinator ensures correct reassembly for downstream KV cache refill without changing model-level semantics. The priority stream allocator exposes a stream affinity table (per-GPU) and a heuristic to prefer mapping small-first chunks to priority streams that have lower expected queuing delay. The scheduler change in runtime/scheduler injects boundaries to interleave compute slices with pending comms based on a predictive cost model calibrated by microbenchmarks. Implementation notes: changes span runtime/tp/allgather_splitter.* (C++), runtime/scheduler/priority_stream_scheduler.* (C++), runtime/nccl/stream_pool.cc (affinity and priority support), serving/flags/config.proto (new runtime flags), tests/bench/tp_allgather_bench.py (microbench harness), and docs/perf/lazy-allgather.md. Backwards compatibility: default is off for private deployments; hosted will enable flag behind a gradual rollout gate after cluster verification. Testing: unit tests for splitter ordering and reassembly, synthetic microbenchmarks on 8xA100 and 4xH100 clusters, integration runs with real workloads used in ENG-3124. Results: 12-18% steady-state throughput increase on small-batch long-seq TP configs, 1.4x reduction in 95th percentile latency during KV cache warmup phases, and 35% fewer NCCL stream stalls observed in trace captures. Checklist: - [x] microbenchmarks and traces - [x] unit and integration tests - [x] docs and rollout notes - [x] feature flag gating - [x] reviewers and perf signoff

review_comments: Ethan Kim: Overall this looks promising; can you add a safety timeout so a missing chunk doesn't block indefinitely? Also please document the memory tax when we buffer partial shards.
Maya Patel: Added chunk timeout (configurable) and documented buffering impact in docs/perf/lazy-allgather.md; timeout defaults to 100ms and is gated by the feature flag.
Sofia Alvarez: Benchmarks look good; request that we add a regression unit that simulates bursty small-sequence workloads to ensure priority streams don't starve background collectives.
Maya Patel: Added synthetic burst test and updated scheduler to degrade priority allocation under sustained background load.
Arjun Rao: Approving pending CI green and a quick run on a 4-node staging cluster to validate cross-node reassembly traces.
